name: Fixturehaus
positioning: Fixturehaus is the matchday football publication that turns fixture lists, previews and scorecards into bold, scannable kit-graphic stories for fans who plan their weekend around kickoff.
audience: Matchday fans aged 18-40 who follow several clubs, check fixtures on their phone between Friday and Monday, and want fast, confident previews rather than long-form punditry.
strategy: Own the 72 hours before kickoff with a fixture board, data-led previews and a free predictor league that builds a weekly ritual. Every format leads with the matchup (VS split, scoreboard, table) so a post reads in under three seconds in the feed. Community features reward opinions and bragging rights, never betting.

contrastPairs.use: large display type and graphics only (not body text)

fonts.mono: Rubik (tabular figures; no mono in brief)

designSystem.spacing: 8px base grid; section padding 64-112px; 64px minimum safe margin on social canvases
designSystem.radius: 10-16px on cards and scoreboards, full pills for CTAs and labels
designSystem.borders: 1px white at 14% for structure; 2-4px Kit Green or Scoreboard Yellow to signal the featured match
designSystem.imagery: Original vector only: tactical boards, floodlight towers, crests and pitch markings. No photography.
designSystem.shapes: Shield crests, diagonal VS splits, circular VS badges, LED digit boxes
designSystem.buttons: Scoreboard Yellow pill with Bebas Neue label and arrow; outline white secondary
designSystem.cards: Deep green panels with a coloured kit-stripe edge; featured items get a green border
designSystem.motifs: Pitch lines at low opacity, VS splits, scoreboards, vertical kit stripes, floodlight radial glows

artDirection: Every creative leads with the matchup: a VS split, a fixture board or a table, set in towering Bebas Neue with Rubik doing the explaining. Night-pitch green is the stage, floodlight glows light it from the top corners, and faint pitch markings anchor the grid. Yellow is reserved for kickoff times and CTAs, red for the away side and SAMPLE labels, green for the home side and data. All clubs, players and numbers are fictional and every story is labelled as a sample.
